why: keeps #87 r3 F2.1; the device kills the worker on its own budget (#199 r1), so the settle time is proof, not a guess

choice: T6 leaves the failure unhandled with requeue-deferred until finished_at + LINK_DROP_BACKOFF_SECONDS[used]

why: consumers compare job-failed-2 by value, so no new stuck reason; worst case bounded at 2 x (6 + 1) runs

choice: choose_device(avoid=) ranks the dropped device last; claim reads the row's latest run end
why: a requeue moves off a dead device when another has room, so a dead device usually costs one cycle

choice: _device_offline always leaves a link-dropped job to _check_job_states

choice: the link-drop detail names the dropped run's worker tag; link_drop_end ignores a drop whose tag the slot no longer names
why: binding at the one read every caller shares (_link_drop_settled, _device_offline, T6) covers the whole class; the reviewer's repro now leaves the takeover running and nothing claimable

choice: T6 frees a failed link-dropped row's slot before falling through to the retry
why: the row left running only once its worker was confirmed gone or past its deadline, so the slot guards nothing; a one-slot device now claims attempt 2

choice: _review_retry_waits runs before the free requeue as before the retry
why: one deferral rule for every T6 requeue of a review; the reviewer's repro now holds the review failed beside the fix
